name: castle_watchtower_base
note: CylinderGeometry(2.5,3,24,16) - 9 m at the foot, 36 m tall (54 m at the site scale of 1.5). One uniform cone taper for the whole shaft; no plinth, no spur. After: plinth, weathered talus, two stages divided by a set-back, near-vertical upper shaft. Segments unchanged at 16.

name: castle_watchtower_corbel
note: CylinderGeometry(3.2,2.5,1,16) - a plain inverted-taper collar 14.4 m across. After: machicolation splay off the tower face, a vertical parapet wall, a chamfered coping the merlons stand on. Segments unchanged at 16.

name: castle_watchtower_merlon
note: NEW - there is no prior geometry, so 'before' is the naive plain block a merlon would otherwise be, which also fixes the envelope the designed one has to hold. 4 sides on purpose: crenellation is the one feature on this tower that must NOT be round.

name: castle_watchtower_spire
note: ConeGeometry(3.5,12,16) - a smooth 10.5 m x 18 m cone whose base ring swallowed the corbel course and the top 1.5 m of the tower. After: a narrow drum that springs from inside the parapet, a soffit sweeping out to a bell-cast eave, then a slender concave spire. Same max radius, same y range; the WIDEST RING MOVES UP 3.4 units so the parapet is no longer buried.

name: castle_gate_turret_body
note: CylinderGeometry(1.5,1.8,12,16) - 5.4 m across at the foot, 18 m tall, one uniform taper and a flat top. After: plinth, talus, near-vertical shaft, a corbelled head that oversails, then a set-in drum for the roof to spring from. Segments unchanged at 16; one geometry now shared by both turrets.

name: castle_gate_turret_cap
note: ConeGeometry(2,5,16) - a smooth 6 m x 7.5 m cone sleeved 2.2 m down over the turret shaft, no eave and no finial. After: a bell-cast eave that oversails the corbelled head, a steeper concave pitch, and a ball-and-spike finial. Same max radius and y range; the widest ring moves up 0.4 unit so the head reads.
